Subject: Pilot next steps — is now the right time?

Hi Anna / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discovery. Quick recap so we have aligned notes and a suggested next step: 

Goals we heard
- Reduce time-to-insight on claims anomalies by 40% for the pilot population
- Integrate inference with your existing ETL (Kafka -> Redshift) and limit PII in payloads

Success criteria for a minimal pilot
- End-to-end run of 5k claims/day with <600ms 95th percentile per request
- Qualitative sign-off from two clinical reviewers on sample outputs

Suggested pilot scope (what Redwood would deliver)
- Dedicated model pool (2x A100-equivalent) for 6 weeks
- Prefix caching for common templates, eval harness for quality checks
- Security questionnaire + SOC2 evidence (we can provide the audit packet)

Next steps I propose
1) I’ll drop the proposed Statement of Work and a mutual action plan (attached).
2) If procurement is okay, schedule a 30-min procurement + security call next week to align on contracts/KMS.
3) Engineering kickoff and access to a sandbox dataset the week after procurement sign-off.

Attachments: redwood-proposal-GFH-v1.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Are you able to confirm whether procurement can meet next week (Wed/Thu)? If not, what timing is better on your side?

If it helps I can include Marissa on the procurement call to run the SLA/commit questions.

Thanks — Jonas

--

Hi Anna / Tom —

Wanted to check the pulse again before I loop Marissa out of the thread. We haven’t heard back on whether the pilot is a Q2 priority. Two quick options from our side so you can choose what fits your roadmap: 

Option A — Fast-track (if this is prioritized)
- Procurement call this week -> sign SOW -> engineering kickoff in 7–10 days
- Redwood will commit a short SLA and a named engineer for onboarding

Option B — Pause and re-scope (if lower priority)
- We’ll pause active scheduling and keep the mutual action plan on file. No cost or signatures required until you’re ready.

If I don’t hear anything by Tue 11 May, is it okay if I close the file on our side and archive the opportunity? We’ll happily reopen when you’re ready, but this helps us keep planning tidy.

If there’s a blocker (security, budget, timing), tell me and I’ll escalate internally to see if we can move the needle.

Best, Jonas

Can you archive the current plan on your side? Please keep the mutual action plan handy; we expect to re-open procurement conversations in early Q3 (target week of July 11). I’ll reintroduce this internally then and reach back out.
